subject.title: Add dependency scanning for package releases

question: Should ClawHub treat high-confidence OSV MAL dependency advisories as install-blocking exact-release trust signals for existing and future package releases?
rationale: This changes the marketplace trust boundary and upgrade behavior for already-published releases; automation can review code shape but cannot own that policy decision.

options.title: Accept MAL blocking after proof
options.body: Require green gates and a live backend scan/backfill proof, then land the PR with MAL dependency advisories driving exact-release quarantine.

options.title: Keep dependency findings advisory-only
options.body: Store and surface dependency findings without letting OSV dependency malware automatically block downloads until maintainers define a separate escalation path.

options.title: Split scanner from blocking policy
options.body: Merge a narrower scanner/backfill foundation first and move install-blocking trust propagation to a follow-up policy PR.

recommendation.title: Accept MAL blocking after proof
recommendation.body: Require green gates and a live backend scan/backfill proof, then land the PR with MAL dependency advisories driving exact-release quarantine.

likelyOwner.reason: The current release trust and quarantine path traces most directly to Patrick-Erichsen's recent merged package security work.
